source: Real headless conversions via scripts/cli-convert.mjs -w pyrite on 2026-08-31. Document: 2013.pdf, 18 pages, book pages 133-150 of a digital (text-layer) internal medicine question bank. Questions 130 and 1-129 of the 'November 2013' paper.
shape: digital text layer; answers marked ONLY by green option text, no key and no letter mark; EVERY page ends mid-question, so 15 questions have choices split across a page break; one question prints its choices a,b,d,e; one marks two options green; the last is cut off by the document's end
gold_comparison: Not run on this document. The 0.2.0 rows below are the same workflow before this change, not a Gold baseline.
grading: Answer letters are POSITIONAL (A = first printed choice), scored by scripts/grade-run.mjs. Q91 (two green options) and Q129 (cut off by the PDF end) are excluded, leaving 128 gradeable of 130.

runs.notes: Two of nine windows numbered their rows against the images they were handed (1,2,3) instead of the document pages the prompt named, so 21 re-read questions failed the one-page deduplication test and shipped a second time under `#2` ids; 20 of them were unflagged and would have imported. The split also kept the weaker sighting as the primary row: Q122 shipped three INVENTED choices with no answer while the correct reading sat beside it under `122#2`. Q114 received Q115's four choices because it flagged itself cut despite carrying all four of its own, producing an 8-option row whose answer index pointed into the wrong half, unflagged.
Same defect, different windows: four of nine renumbered here rather than two. Q14 was lost entirely.

Run 1's stored window responses reassembled through 0.3.0 with no request at all. This is the controlled measurement: identical model output, only the local rules changed. 155 rows to exactly the document's 130, every duplicate and fragment gone, five answers recovered. Replaying run 2 the same way: 161 rows to 130, 118 correct to 121.

Ten requests, against eleven and nine for 0.2.0 on the same document: the budget did not move, because every rule added here reads data the run already had. Q86's stem was never returned by any window this run — a model recall miss, not an assembly one — and its orphaned choices stayed a visible flagged fragment rather than being welded onto a neighbour or dropped.

gate.no_incorrect_key_answer: not exercised; this document has no separate key
gate.ambiguous_rows_flagged: improved, still failing: 3 wrong answers export unflagged (Q26, Q43, Q66). Nothing in Pyrite can catch a mark the model misread, since there is no second reading of any page.

caveats: Two runs of 0.2.0, one of 0.3.0, plus two replays. The replay is the controlled comparison; the fresh run is the end-to-end confirmation.

Q93 regressed from blank to wrong. Deduplication prefers an answered sighting over a blank one, so once the two sightings merge the model's misread wins. The row stays flagged options_cut_at_page_break and does not export, but the number moved the wrong way and the cause is understood, not accidental.

Q26 and Q43 look like subject knowledge overriding the page: in both the model returned the textbook answer rather than the green one, and Q43 was wrong in all three runs. Two cases is not proof, but it is the failure Pyrite's safety rule forbids and no local rule can detect it.
The answer marking here is green text with no letter, tick or highlighter. That Pyrite reads it at all is worth recording; it is not evidence about scanned or handwritten marks.
The separate answer-key PDF path is untouched by this change and still has no end-to-end verification on a real key document.
